definition: A system composed of multiple AI agents that interact, communicate, or collaborate (and sometimes compete) to accomplish tasks.
details: Multi-agent LLM systems can divide labor across specialized sub-agents (e.g., a planner, a coder, a reviewer), potentially improving robustness and task decomposition compared to a single monolithic agent.
story: Picture hiring a brilliant new assistant on their first morning — smart, motivated, but with no idea how anything in your office actually works. In plain words: A system composed of multiple AI agents that interact, communicate, or collaborate (and sometimes compete) to accomplish tasks. Here is how it actually plays out: Multi-agent LLM systems can divide labor across specialized sub-agents (e.g., a planner, a coder, a reviewer), potentially improving robustness and task decomposition compared to a single monolithic agent. The model stops being a one-shot answer machine and becomes a coworker that checks its own work. That loop of reason, act, and observe is Multi-Agent System.
